topics.label: Start
topics.title: Start investigating
paragraphs: You are an independent investigator working from the WHOAMI desktop. Read the client's message first, then follow the evidence across the available apps.
Search records, compare sources, and build a timeline. A useful conclusion should be supported by several independent pieces of evidence.
The desktop is a simulation: your commands only affect this case and never run on your computer or contact real services.

items.description: Select an app in the dock to open it. Drag windows by their title bars; minimize, maximize, close, or resize them with the window controls.
Use the ? button beside the clock or open Handbook from the dock to return to these instructions.
Start with what is already available, then follow names, dates, accounts, locations, and other details into related records.
Evidence may be public, found in an app, or locked behind a simulated account or target. Keep track of what you have discovered and downloaded.

topics.label: Terminal
topics.title: The case terminal
paragraphs: The terminal is a simulated command interface for the fictional case. It does not provide access to your computer, the internet, or real systems.
Type a command and press Enter. Use the up and down arrows to recall previous commands. The terminal history and investigation progress are saved for this case.

topics.label: How to hack
topics.title: Unlocking simulated records
paragraphs: Some fictional records require a simulated access path. Follow the requirements shown by the case; not every record uses every step.

topics.label: Passwords
topics.title: Finding passwords and clues
paragraphs: Passwords are part of the investigation. The handbook does not contain case passwords: look for clues in evidence, messages, public posts, and account records.
A clue may point to a meaningful word, date, or combination. Treat it as a lead and verify it against the evidence rather than trying unrelated guesses.

items.description: Use login with the service, account, and password supported by the case records. A failed login means the credentials or account do not match.
For encrypted archives, add a discovered clue to your wordlist and run crack with --wordlist mine. Only clues you collected in-game are checked.
Once an archive is unlocked, extract it with unzip. Its contents then become available in Files.
